changes.label: Operating Expenses › Payroll & Benefits
changes.cause: Isla Fraser, Priya Chandra and Rhys Owen were each paid salary twice in the month: once mid-month and again on the usual payday. This may be a duplicate run or an off-cycle payment. There was also a one-off recruitment placement fee to Fathom Talent Partners, a new kind of cost for this category. The Remote People contractor payroll ran as normal.

changes.label: Operating Expenses › Rent
changes.cause: The usual monthly WeWork desk payment went out at the start of the month as before. Two more identical WeWork desk-rental direct debits were then taken on the same day mid-month. This is either extra desks being added or a duplicate charge to dispute with WeWork.

changes.label: Operating Expenses › Subscriptions
changes.cause: A new JetBrains All Products licence was bought and coded to prepayments, so it looks like an annual upfront purchase. A new BCS membership and a BCS learning charge were added. Figma charged its organisation plan several times plus extra professional seats, which may be duplicate billing. Sentry stays a large recurring cost.

changes.label: Financial Items › Capital Investments
changes.cause: There were one-off equipment purchases from two new vendors: computer hardware from the Apple Store and ergonomic office equipment from Posturite. Both have receipts and are coded to fixed-asset accounts.

changes.label: Operating Expenses › Legal & Professional Fees
changes.cause: Harrison & Webb Solicitors billed well above their usual monthly level. A new professional indemnity insurance renewal from Meridian Insurance Brokers also landed in this category, though it really belongs under Insurance. Connolly Accountants' bookkeeping fee was unchanged.

sections.title: What changed
sections.body_filled:
Total spend was £162,334, up £29,819 (+22.5%).

Payroll & Benefits rose £11,667 (+20.3%). Isla Fraser (£8,700), Priya Chandra (£7,100) and Rhys Owen (£7,800) each received two salary payments, and there was a one-off recruitment placement fee.

Rent rose +187.2% to £6,750 because of extra WeWork direct debits on top of the normal desk fee.

Subscriptions rose +92.0%, driven by a new JetBrains licence (£1,990), a new BCS membership (£790) and repeated Figma charges.

Capital investments were £4,775: one-off equipment from Apple (£2,399) and Posturite (£2,376).

Legal & Professional Fees rose +39.3%. Harrison & Webb billed £4,900, and a new PI insurance renewal (£1,240) is temporarily sitting in this category.

sections.title: Risks & asks
sections.body_filled: We need to confirm whether the second salary run for Isla Fraser, Priya Chandra and Rhys Owen was intentional. We also need to confirm whether the extra WeWork and Figma charges are duplicates, and claw them back if so. An unknown vendor charged a management fee with no invoice: please identify it or dispute it. Team members should upload missing receipts so the backlog shrinks before year-end. Several of this month's increases look one-off, so underlying burn should come back down if those duplicates are confirmed.
